title: Best Cartoon Illustrators (2026): Custom Cartoons and Characters
description: How to hire a cartoon illustrator for portraits, mascots, comics or marketing: rights, files, how to brief it, what drives the price and red flags.
intro: Cartoon illustrators draw people, characters, mascots and scenes in a fun, simplified style. Cartoons work well for gifts, social media, brand mascots, comics and explainer visuals. Projects go wrong when the style is not agreed, the likeness is off in a portrait, or the license does not cover commercial use. This guide helps you get cartoon art that fits your purpose.

faq.q: Can I use the cartoon for my business?
faq.a: Only if the license allows commercial use. Personal gifts usually need no commercial license; logos, products and ads do.

faq.q: How do I get a good likeness in a cartoon portrait?
faq.a: Send several clear, well-lit photos from different angles and mention features that matter, such as hairstyle, glasses or a typical expression.
Usually high-resolution PNG and JPG. For printing large or editing, ask for the layered source file or a vector version.

faq.q: Can the character be used in several poses?
faq.a: Many illustrators offer extra poses or a character sheet. This is useful if the character will appear across a brand or a story.
Check the number of revisions and at which stage they apply. Changes are easiest at the sketch stage.
